answer: Sybil resistance comes from bonded vouching: a new agent cannot act until an established sponsor stakes collateral on its behalf, and that stake is slashed if the newcomer cheats. Picture reputation as a slope climbing from a grassy knoll toward a distant horizon; each fake identity an attacker spins up needs its own locked onyx deposit plus a sponsor risking real funds. Minting a thousand sybils therefore costs a thousand bonds and a thousand sponsors with skin in the game, so the flood never turns a profit.
